renderer: Deployed 0.9.4 Web canvas-preview engine, new headless Chromium 117 for every job; code generation, compile, React render, DOM snapshot, 640x360 PNG and decoded pixel check for each job. Offline replay of pinned project/library snapshots, locally served static assets and required Google fonts. Excludes queue delay, online snapshot preparation, CDN WAN time and final upload. Diagnostic PNG decode/check included in end-to-end time.
hardware: Intel Pentium Gold 8505, Linux x86_64; 15763 MiB RAM, 14023 MiB swap. Initial observation MemAvailable 3947 MiB, swap used 7204 MiB.
isolation: One render job at a time. Default 1 CPU quota, separate 2 CPU experiment, 1280 MiB cgroup hard memory limit, swap disabled for rendering container. Save replay uses separate private Postgres and exact production saveProjectRev handler, isolated synthetic user, local directory and socket responses, one field changed on a 1.06 MB model and actual revision committed over loopback HTTP at 2 s intervals. Test API 1.5 CPU and 1100 MiB, test PostgreSQL 1 CPU and 320 MiB. No writes to production business projects.
sampling: Render cgroup memory.peak includes node harness/loopback static delivery and Chromium, reported for each fresh container. Chrome-only PSS sampled across browser process tree every 500 ms on B/C and largest runs. CPU seconds are cgroup usage from browser launch to verified image, same interval as elapsed time. Save p95 nearest rank, warmup excluded, only fully in-window saves in render groups. AB blocks interleaved; naturally varying co-resident service load. Host swap activity and PSI are host-wide, not attributable to one container.

deadlineExperiment: For large90A and large90B only, the local HTTP fixture changed the exact syncPreview wait in the served preview engine JS from 30000 ms to 90000 ms. Production assets and configuration were untouched. Fresh preview compiler and Chromium each run.
scope: Read-only inventory found 11 active projects/templates with saved main revision lengths after excluding registered library projects; all 11 had non-null lengths. The largest was selected. Business save model was the same 4-board benchmark in every block; no simulated network failure, production authentication, sustained queue, or peak user concurrency.
